text:
andrew: FWIW I dug into the p99 spikes. Root cause is compaction running immediately on idle and stealing bandwidth from small request hotpaths. Thinking tenant-scoped defrag budgets might help.

maria: Can you sketch how budgets work?

andrew: Idea: each tenant gets a small 'compaction credit' bucket (ms/sec). When tenant is active credits drain. When idle credits accumulate up to a cap. Evictor consumes credits to run compaction; if credits exhausted, compaction must stop or yield. Credits reset slower for low-priority tenants.

lee: That plus a global defrag window seems good. Also add interrupt-safe compaction: make compaction chunked with checkpoints at chunk boundaries so we can resume or abort without corrupting slab metadata.

xia: For chunking: prefer fixed-chunk byte size (~64KB) and mark progress in a small per-slab journal entry. On preempt, write a tombstone and another worker continues later. Avoid long-held locks.

andrew: Also propose a tiny preemption API: 
```
// returns a short token handled by evictor threads
string token = evictor.acquire_run_token(int want_ms, int tenant_id, int priority);
// evictor checks periodically: bool cont = evictor.token_heartbeat(token);
// if false, stop asap and persist progress marker
```
This keeps the allocate path lock-free.

maria: Telemetry we need: tenant_compaction_credit_ms, compaction_chunks_started, compaction_chunks_completed, compaction_abort_reasons, compaction_resume_count, preempt_heartbeats, small_req_p50/p95/p99_by_tenant.

xia: Prefetch nuance: when request marks context as "short", do conservative KV/attention prefetch (prefetch only first N spans with heuristics). For "long" contexts prefetch more aggressively. Add request hint: prefetch_profile:short|balanced|aggressive.

lee: Autotune idea: monitor small_req_p99 and compaction_cost_per_gb. If p99 rises above SLO, reduce credit refill rate or widen defrag window for affected tenants. If cost per token rises too much, narrow window to recover packing. Keep a safety floor so fragmentation never grows unbounded.

andrew: Ops knobs: --tenant-defrag-credits-ms-per-sec, --global-defrag-window-ms, --compaction-chunk-bytes, --compaction-heartbeat-interval-ms, --compaction-max-run-ms. Per-tenant overrides in config.

maria: Need correctness note: compaction must be idempotent. If interrupted we must be able to resume without double-free or leak. Journal entries + versioned slab headers should handle this. Add a unit test that simulates random preemption.

xia: Rollout plan: 1) implement credits + token API behind feature flag, 2) canary 1% tenants with verbose telemetry, 3) expand to 10% with autotune off, 4) enable autotune for a small cohort, 5) full rollout. Include kill-switch to disable credits and fall back to previous compactor.

lee: I'll PR the token API and a small in-memory simulator to validate credit behavior. Planning microbench: 50ms bursts every 300ms vs steady background. Measure p99, compaction work saved, and fragmentation delta.

andrew: I'll draft a short RFC with API, metrics, failure modes, and test plan. Tagging @maria @xia.

infra-bot: created checklist /infra/checks/defrag-credits-RFC-1833331234 4cb 6 checks pending

maria: One subtlety: shared GPUs with bursty tenants could starve others if we give credits per tenant. Maybe add a pool-level throttler so one noisy tenant can't hog compaction slot.

andrew: Good call. Add pool_compaction_weight and a small fairness token-bucket at pool-level.

xia: I'll add the compaction-chunk recovery doc and sketch journal format.

lee: will post the prototype PR later today. :thumbsup:
